blocks.text: 我们宣布在数学、计算机科学和物理学领域的三项新发现，分别涉及调和分析、复杂性理论和量子场论。

inlines.text: 我们宣布在数学、计算机科学和物理学领域的三项新发现，分别涉及调和分析、复杂性理论和量子场论。

blocks.text: 我们的发布流程会持续根据相关学术社区的反馈而演进。在我们看来，这些手稿最好被理解为一种原始研究数据。为了将这些原始研究数据转化为科学理解，在本次发布中我们正在尝试一种新方法。我们联系了外部专家，请他们担任引导者，组织团队来理解这些新结果。他们建议了三种不同的发布策略：

inlines.text: 我们的发布流程会持续根据相关学术社区的反馈而演进。在我们看来，这些手稿最好被理解为一种原始研究数据。为了将这些原始研究数据转化为科学理解，在本次发布中我们正在尝试一种新方法。我们联系了外部专家，请他们担任引导者，组织团队来理解这些新结果。他们建议了三种不同的发布策略：
对于数学成果，发布 AI 输出，让研究人员自由组织自己的努力来解释该结果。
对于计算机科学成果，组建一个外部合作团队来解释该结果，同时将 AI 输出公开，供任何人检查和在此基础上继续研究。
对于物理学成果，组建一个外部合作团队，并在材料发布上听从他们的意见。

blocks.text: 我们尚不清楚这三种方法中哪一种最有用，我们欢迎就哪些做法有效、哪些可以改进提供反馈。

blocks.text: 外部合作将遵循四项原则：

inlines.text: 外部合作将遵循四项原则：
透明度。
我们对我们合作的存在保持透明。参与者不会被要求签署保密协议，并可自由讨论工作、分享中间成果并发表他们的结论。
不寻求学术荣誉。
我们不为我们内部模型产生的发现寻求学术荣誉。邀请研究人员帮助管理合作，也不意味着他们或其工作组做出了原始发现。
**认可。**该团队应因其建立的理解、撰写的文稿以及创建的其他材料而获得认可。该团队还将帮助确保工作适当归功于其所借鉴的研究人员、技术和想法。
**独立性。**参与是自愿且无报酬的。工作组成员独立参与，其结论属于他们自己。他们不代表 OpenAI 发言，OpenAI 也不代表他们发言。

blocks.text: 我们将把与这些结果相关的材料和产物移交给各合作团队。对于计算机科学合作，该团队已决定立即公开自然语言证明和 Lean 形式化，我们正直接将其发布到我们的 GitHub 仓库。对于物理学合作，该团队已决定暂不发布 AI 生成的产物，而是自行撰写。

blocks.text: 所有这些方法都涉及权衡。一方面，合作使专家能够促进对结果的解读，并将其置于更广泛的学术背景中。另一方面，选择初始引导者必然会影响谁先参与，并造成信息不对称。我们欢迎就如何扩大参与、使这一过程更有用提供反馈。

blocks.text: 局部平滑与 Kakeya 猜想

inlines.text: 局部平滑与 Kakeya 猜想

blocks.text: 这个数学结果涉及调和分析。1991年，Sogge 提出了局部光滑猜想，该猜想关注波在聚焦时的行为。具体而言，该猜想指出，最极端的聚焦必然是短暂的。在典型随机时刻的聚焦量总是远小于最坏情况下可能发生的聚焦量。这是贯穿数学的一个常见模式：最坏情况下可能发生的情形比平均之后观察到的情形更为极端。由于这一猜想现象的根本性，它也在整个数学分析中具有广泛的影响。例如，它蕴含 Kakeya 猜想和 Stein 限制猜想。

blocks.text: 2019年，Guth、Wang 和 Zhang⁠（在新窗口中打开）证明了两个空间维度下的局部光滑猜想。2025年，Wang 和 Zahl⁠（在新窗口中打开）证明了三维修下的 Kakeya 猜想。我们的模型给出了任意维度下局部光滑猜想的证明，因而也在所有维度上解决了 Kakeya 猜想和 Stein 限制猜想。新证明基于一个新颖的辅助偏微分方程。

blocks.text: 指数时间假说为假

inlines.text: 指数时间假说为假

blocks.text: 该计算机科学合作将理解并解释一个关于指数时间假说（ETH）的结果，这是一个关于布尔公式可满足性计算复杂性的长期猜想，该问题与 P vs. NP 问题密切相关。ETH 一直被广泛认为是真的，并已在数百篇论文中用于推导条件计算硬度结果，涵盖图论、计算生物学、数据库、计算几何等广泛领域。令人惊讶的是，我们的系统最近证明了 ETH 为假，该结果随后在 Lean 中得到了验证。对 ETH 的否证重新开启了关于这些任务能变得多快的问题，并可能有助于指导寻找更好的算法。找到此类算法，并将理论进展转化为实际改进，将需要大量进一步研究。

inlines.text: 量子色动力学的存在性与标准模型的完备化

blocks.text: 该物理合作组将理解并解释一项结果，该结果为四维中包含规范场和费米子的某些相互作用量子场论提供了数学上严格的存在性证明，其中包括量子色动力学（QCD）以及粒子物理学标准模型的统一完备化。我们的工作建立在构造性量子场论中Balaban 的方法⁠（在新窗口打开）之上。作为一个子问题，这项工作还包括纯 Yang–Mills 理论存在性的证明，该问题是量子 Yang–Mills 理论 Clay 数学研究所千禧年大奖难题⁠（在新窗口打开）的一部分。

blocks.text: 标准模型描述了基本亚原子粒子在四种基本力中除引力外的三种力下的相互作用。该存在性证明涉及最简单的包含标准模型规范场和费米子的大统一理论（因为标准模型本身无法外推到任意短的距离）。QCD 描述了夸克和胶子等粒子通过强相互作用的相互作用。纯 Yang–Mills 理论仅描述胶子（即力载体）的自相互作用，而不描述夸克等物质。

inlines.text: Our release process continues to evolve in response to feedback from the associated academic communities. In our view, these manuscripts are best understood as a form of raw research data. To convert this raw research data into scientific understanding, in this release we are experimenting with a new approach. We reached out to external experts and asked them to act as shepherds, organizing groups to understand the new results. They advised three different release strategies:
For the math result, release the AI output, leaving researchers free to organize their own efforts to explain the result.
For the computer science result, form an external group of collaborators to explain the result, while making the AI output publicly available for anyone to examine and build on.
For the physics result, form an external group of collaborators and defer to them on the release of materials.

blocks.text: We do not yet know which of these three approaches will be most useful, and we welcome feedback on what works and what we can improve.

blocks.text: The external collaborations will follow four principles:

inlines.text: The external collaborations will follow four principles:
Transparency.

We are transparent about the existence of our collaborations. Participants will not be asked to sign nondisclosure agreements and will be free to discuss the work, share intermediate products, and publish their conclusions.
No Academic Credit.

We do not seek academic credit for the discoveries produced by our internal models. Inviting a researcher to help steward a collaboration also does not imply that they or their working group made the original discovery.

**Recognition.**This group should receive recognition for the understanding they develop, the writeups they author, and the other materials they create. The group will also help ensure that the work appropriately credits researchers, techniques, and ideas that it draws on.

**Independence.**Participation is voluntary and unpaid. Working-group members participate independently, and their conclusions are their own. They do not speak on behalf of OpenAI, and OpenAI does not speak on their behalf.

For the physics collaboration, the group has decided to hold off on releasing the AI-produced artifacts and instead work on writing it up themselves.

blocks.text: All of these approaches involve tradeoffs. On the one hand, the collaborations empower experts to foster unpacking the results and contextualizing them in the broader academic community. On the other hand, choosing initial shepherds necessarily shapes who gets involved first and creates asymmetry of information. We welcome feedback on how to broaden participation and make this process more useful.

blocks.text: Local smoothing and the Kakeya conjecture

inlines.text: Local smoothing and the Kakeya conjecture

blocks.text: The result in mathematics concerns harmonic analysis. In 1991, Sogge proposed the local smoothing conjecture, which concerns the behavior of waves as they become focused. In particular, the conjecture states that the most extreme focusing must be short-lived. The amount of focusing at a typical random time is always much smaller than what can happen at the worst-case time. This is a familiar pattern throughout mathematics: what can happen in the worst case is more extreme than what is observed after averaging. Because of how fundamental this conjectured phenomenon is, it also has wide ranging implications throughout mathematical analysis. For instance, it implies the Kakeya conjecture and Stein’s restriction conjecture.

blocks.text: In 2019, Guth, Wang, and Zhang⁠(opens in a new window) proved the local smoothing conjecture in two spatial dimensions. In 2025, Wang and Zahl⁠(opens in a new window) proved the Kakeya conjecture in three dimensions. Our models produced a proof of the local smoothing conjecture in every dimension and therefore also resolve the Kakeya conjecture and Stein’s restriction conjecture in all dimensions. The new proof is based on a novel auxiliary partial differential equation.

blocks.text: The Exponential Time Hypothesis is false

inlines.text: The Exponential Time Hypothesis is false

blocks.text: The computer science collaboration will understand and explain a result concerning the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), a longstanding conjecture about the computational complexity of Boolean formula satisfiability, a problem deeply related to the P vs. NP problem. The ETH has been widely believed to be true, and has been used in hundreds of papers to derive conditional computational hardness results across a wide variety of fields including graph theory, computational biology, databases, computational geometry, and more. Surprisingly, our system has recently proved that the ETH is false, a result that was subsequently verified in Lean. The refutation of the ETH reopens questions about how much faster these tasks could become, and may help guide the search for better algorithms. Finding such algorithms, and turning theoretical advances into practical improvements, will require significant further research.

We hope that humans with AI can provide new understanding in this field, and shed light on the inherent capabilities and limits of efficient computation.

blocks.text: Existence of quantum chromodynamics and completions of the Standard Model

inlines.text: Existence of quantum chromodynamics and completions of the Standard Model

blocks.text: The physics collaboration will understand and explain a result that gives a mathematically rigorous existence proof of certain interacting quantum field theories containing gauge fields and fermions in four dimensions, including Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and a unified completion of the Standard Model of particle physics. Our work builds on Balaban’s approach⁠(opens in a new window) in constructive quantum field theory. As a subproblem, this work also includes a proof of the existence of pure Yang–Mills theory, which is part of the Quantum Yang–Mills Theory Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize problem⁠(opens in a new window).

blocks.text: The Standard Model describes the interaction of fundamental subatomic particles for three of the four fundamental forces, excepting gravity. The existence proof pertains to the simplest grand unified theory that includes the gauge fields and fermions of the Standard Model (as the Standard Model itself cannot be extrapolated to arbitrarily short distances). QCD describes the interaction of particles such as quarks and gluons via the strong force. Pure Yang–Mills theory only describes the self-interactions of the gluons, the force carriers, rather than matter such as quarks.

blocks.text: David Gross will lead a group including Michael Douglas, Arthur Jaffe, Igor Klebanov, and Nikita Nekrasov that will shepherd this work.

inlines.text: David Gross will lead a group including Michael Douglas, Arthur Jaffe, Igor Klebanov, and Nikita Nekrasov that will shepherd this work.
Gross’s 1973 work on asymptotic freedom in Yang-Mills theories helped establish QCD as the theory of the strong interactions and earned him a share of the
2004 Nobel Prize in Physics⁠(opens in a new window)
. Asymptotic freedom is also the key mechanism underlying the existence of these theories as mathematically rigorous objects.
Jaffe formulated the
Quantum Yang-Mills Theory Millenium Prize problem⁠(opens in a new window)
with Witten and also envisioned the idea of Millennium Prize problems and co-founded the Clay Mathematics Institute.
Douglas has already been a steward of this problem over the last 20 years,
reporting on its status in 2004⁠(opens in a new window)
and then providing a
comprehensive update on the progress⁠(opens in a new window)
at the beginning of this year.
Klebanov helped pioneer the application of gauge–string duality to confinement, an important property of QCD, and now directs the
Simons Collaboration on Confinement and QCD Strings⁠(opens in a new window)
Nekrasov has done groundbreaking work on exact methods for generalizations of Yang–Mills theory and won the Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics in 2023.

blocks.text: Our models produced a natural language proof for Yang–Mills existence on September 9th, 2026, and then subsequently produced a proof for QCD on September 18th, 2026. Given the length and complexity of the work, we postponed release until the Lean formalization completed. We finished our formalization of Yang–Mills’ existence on October 16th, 2026, which led us to develop the collaboration described here.
